chapter: Leaving New York, jazz styles and religion
title: Against horns in church; his church arrangements
summary: Smith says only organ, piano and voices belong in church, but wrote arrangements for a friend's church band.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: all right with me. I told my friend, who died, (?) Phillips... He had a little band around here and I played with him. We played a whole lot of good jobs and everything. He'd go down there and run the service down in the church. He belonged there too. He's a big deacon there. So he tried to get me there. I said, 'Well, you get somebody to play bass(?). I don't believe in no horn being in church."

No. I said, "It don't even sound right. What I love in the church is organ's all right and the piano, you've got to have that. But them horns and things, guitars and things like that, I don't believe in it." And I said, "Furthermore, it doesn't sound like the church if you don't have the voices singing." You take one of them choirs there. If you've got them arranged right and have good singers, it will sound 100 percent better. I said, "The closest thing to a voice is violins -- a bunch of violins. If you can get your choir and violins, then it sounds good." But I said, "I won't go in there." And I wrote two or three little arrangements for him to play down at the church. I'll go down and sit and listen to them play. It was all right. It sounded all right. He had yelling(?) and everything.
What was the instrumentation you made the arrangements for?
It had tenor sax, trumpet, guitar, drums... A

couple of sax. It didn't have no trombone. It had a couple of trumpets. About seven or eight of them. Then ...(?).... a boy named Lee Wilson. He played very good. He was a very good piano player. And he'd be sitting up there in the church playing the piano. He didn't have drums! You see, all that to contend with. Because see, the people out there in the church, they didn't pay no attention, they didn't know, but I've seen(?) it. He loved it. That's what killed him. Yeah. Sure did, in Hot Springs, Arkansas.
